title: George Lewis's clarinet playing, tone and vibrato
summary: Sid's view of George Lewis's ideas, tone and limited study, plus clarinet tuning.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Yeah. And I agree, I think it did get too heavy. Yes, it did. And what did you think about George's, George's own playing as a clarinet player? What did you think?

George had a wealth of ideas. He had a wealth of ideas. None of these, uh, not just George, but none of these colored musicians. Two schools. They're not two schools. They, they didn't make any great study of their horn. And I had a clarinet player, I can't recall his name, that worked here on an off night with a band for me. And I told him one time he had to tune his clarinet because he was terribly sharp, you know? And he said, you can't tune a clarinet, Mr. Sid, you see? And I said, you're mistaken that with an oboe or something else, you see? But you can tune a clarinet. And I showed him how to do it. And I think he had played 30, 35 years and he never bothered to tune that clarinet. He would try to lip it, whether sharp or flat, he'd try to lip it into tune, you see? So actually not too many of them were proficient. That wasn't George, really.

No, indeed it wasn't George. Because George sometimes did have a tendency to play a little sharp, you know? Yeah, it wasn't George. Especially if he had a piano. So he, um... What did you think of George's tone?

George had a good sound and most of them get a... Most colored musicians I find are not at their best on the clarinet because they'll get an anti-vibrata, an awfully fast vibrata. And a thin tone, more or less. And I found George was George's clarinet and for the old time, I guess we can call him that, New Orleans musician was probably more pleasing than anyone I've heard about him. He had a wealth of good ideas. He, uh, had a pretty fair command of his instrument. He was no master of the clarinet, but he would get those hands and find those notes some kind of way. Yeah. Whereas if he had a better study of the clarinet, had had a better study of the clarinet, he would have known the different figurines that he could substitute, you know? Yeah. Because I used to watch him. But, uh, George's a beautiful clarinet man. Beautiful man. But he did have a name of a brighter.

Nanny vibrata. Nanny. It's a little, uh, whether vibrata is a little too, uh, exaggerated or too fast, you see. Because it should be controlled. But, uh, many of them have that, whether it's trumpet or trombone or, uh, or clarinet.
